description:
FILED s422 (probe residue of #419; LOUD, not silent-wrong).

A pattern holding a code point above U+10FFFF cannot be compiled by cl-ppcre,
and PCL prints cl-ppcre's own message on stderr and treats the match as
false:

    no warnings;
    print "m:", ("\x{41}" =~ /\x{4000000}/ ? 1 : 0), "\n";

  perl:  m:0
  PCL:   warning: Regex syntax error: Unknown token question-mark in parse tree.
         m:0

The VALUE agrees with perl in every probed shape (s422: the bare pattern
above; `qr/[\x{4000001}\x{4000003}\x{4000005}]+/` against "x" — compiles
silently and answers 0, as perl does; `/a[\x{110000}]?bc/` against "abc" — 1
in both), and it cannot diverge on a MATCH, because after #419 no PCL string
can hold such a character to match against.  So this is a message-quality
item, not a correctness one:

  * the text is cl-ppcre's, not PCL's — it does not say which pattern, does
    not carry the `PCL:` prefix the rule-12 announce family uses
    (%p-announce-unsupported), and is not deduped, so a pattern inside a loop
    prints once per compile;
  * a stderr line fails a row under the #355 stderr-aware Pl/t helper.

Fix shape: where the regex compiler catches cl-ppcre's parse failure, route
the report through %p-announce-unsupported ("regex", the pattern) with a
docs/not-supported.md pointer to "Code points above U+10FFFF", keeping the
false result.  Filler-sized; the s366 filler rule applies.
title: A >U+10FFFF code point in a PATTERN leaks cl-ppcre's own warning instead of a PCL announce
